subject: Prefetch hit-plan and budget qualification for Skyline Health
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: prefetch hit-plan, rough budget range + ask on volumes

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + a couple items we need to lock down to get you a target price: 

Summary from call (short):
- Skyline use case: clinical summarization + triage prompts for clinician-facing app, high concurrency during day shift.
- Typical prompt pattern: user question (avg ~18–60 tokens) + a 30–80 token template/prefix that’s shared across many requests.
- Immediate need: pilot across 1 region (us-west), goal to validate latency and cost over a 3-month window.

Numbers we need from you to finalize model: please confirm these if the ballpark below is correct or update:
- Monthly token volume: ~150M tokens/month (baseline) — is this correct?
- Peak days: ~7–9M tokens/day during month-end/peak.
- Active unique prompts that are highly repetitive (eligible for prefetch/prefix cache): ~40–50% of traffic?
- Budget band you have in mind for production: you mentioned $100–140k/month?

Caching/prefetch assumptions we would use for a conservative quote:
- Prefetch/prefix layer: we assume a persistent prefix cache (customer-specific templates) of ~40 tokens on average.
- Conservative hit-rate baseline: 30% (safe), mid-case 45%, optimistic 60%.
- We also model a warm-session layer (session KV warmups) that can add ~5–10% additional effective coverage for returning users.

What I’ll do next: put together a short, 1-page cost model that shows effective $/1M tokens at 30/45/60% hit rates and two price options (pilot vs committed). Attached the usage export you mentioned (please confirm) so our finance ops can sanity-check.

Attachments: Skyline_MLP_usage_report.csv (export you sent during demo) — please confirm this file is representative of 1 month of baseline traffic.

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm monthly and peak token assumptions above (or send corrected numbers).
2) Confirm whether you prefer a 3-month pilot (no commit) or a 6-month pilot with a small reserved commit.
3) Procurement: best contact + rough lead time for MSA/PO.

Thanks — I’ll await your confirmation and will loop Kar to build a model once we have the numbers.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Torres <atorres@skylinehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prefetch hit-plan, rough budget range + ask on volumes

Mina — thanks for the recap, that aligns closely. Quick clarifications and the team's constraints: 

Confirmed numbers: 
- Baseline tokens: ~150M tokens/month (we can push to 200M in growth scenarios within 6 months).
- Peak: roughly 8M tokens/day is a realistic peak number.
- Repetitive prompt share: around 45% of calls use the same 30–50 token prompt fragment (templates + instructions).
- Current internal budget for this category: ~$120k/month (upper bound approval for pilot → production).

Procurement note: Procurement is on this thread — typical review is 2–3 weeks after a final SOW; they will want an itemized cost table and an example invoice.

One ask: can you show effective $/1M tokens after factoring in prefetch hit rates at 30/45/60%? Also show the impact of a 40-token persistent prefix vs a 10-token session warm layer only.

If we can see a credible $/1M in the $400–600 range at a mid-case hit rate, I can push this up for an exec sign.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Torres
Director, Engineering — AI Platform
Skyline Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: prefetch hit-plan, rough budget range + ask on volumes

Karthik / Ben — forwarding Alex's confirmation. Key asks below; can you run a quick model and confirm which pricing options we should propose?

Customer asks:
- Baseline: 150M tokens/month, peak ~8M/day.
- Repetitive prefix share: ~45% (they cited 30–50% on call).
- Budget target: ~$120k/month.

Model asks (priority):
1) Effective $/1M tokens at hit rates 30%, 45% (mid), 60% factoring:
   - Raw per-token price (our hosted list) assume $850/1M tokens as example baseline for the model (you can adjust).
   - Persistent prefix: assume average 40 tokens saved on prefix hits.
   - Session warm layer: assume additional 7% effective coverage if enabled.
2) Pilot options to recommend:
   - No-commit 3-month pilot (list pricing + small pilot discount).
   - 6-month small reserved capacity with tiered discount to hit $450–550/1M depending on commit.
3) Operational note: show latency SLO implications for using prefix caching vs purely live inference (they care about 200–300ms tail).

Please reply with a 1-paragraph recommendation and a table (or bullet numbers) we can send to Alex + Procurement.

Thanks — Mina

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: prefetch hit-plan, rough budget range + ask on volumes

Mina / Karthik — quick model and recommendation (attachments: SaaS_PRICING_DRAFT_v2.pdf stub). Numbers below are illustrative but conservative.

Assumptions for model:
- Raw hosted list price (baseline): $850 / 1M tokens (this is our non-committed per-token equivalent for the target model).
- Prefix size: 40 tokens saved per prefix hit.
- Average total tokens per call: 60 tokens (includes user prompt + model reply average).
- Session warm layer adds a flat +7% effective hit coverage when enabled.

Calculations (simplified):
- Effective tokens billed per call without caching: 60 tokens → baseline cost per call = 60/1e6 * $850 = $0.051
- With prefix hit (40 tokens): billed tokens = 20 tokens → per-call cost = 20/1e6 * $850 = $0.017

Effective $/1M tokens at hit rates (mid-case = 45%):
- 30% hit rate: effective price = $850 * (1 - (0.30 * 40/60) - (0.07 * 0.30 * 40/60)) ≈ $620 / 1M tokens
- 45% hit rate: effective price ≈ $490 / 1M tokens
- 60% hit rate: effective price ≈ $360 / 1M tokens
(Notes: session warm adds ~7% extra effective coverage layered on top of prefix hits in the model above.)

Recommendation:
- Pilot approach: propose a 3-month pilot at $550 / 1M (pilot discount off list) with a 10% credits cap and usage reporting; this aligns with Alex's $400–600 target at mid-case if they enable prefix caching and session warm.
- Committed approach: offer $450 / 1M for a 6-month reserved commit (minimum 120M tokens/month commit), with an SLA and a migration support credit. This pushes expected cost into the $420–480 band in mid/optimistic hit-rate cases.

Operational callouts:
- Prefix caching adds minimal tail latency if using persistent cache co-located with inference nodes; expect median latency unchanged and 95p tail increase of ~30–60ms if cache misses force KV warmups. We'll propose a short engineering checklist to validate tail latency during pilot.
- We should include a one-pager cost table + example invoice for Procurement.

Next actions I can take:
1) Finalize a 1-page cost table for Alex + Procurement (I attached SaaS_PRICING_DRAFT_v2.pdf stub).
2) Create a pilot SOW draft and send to Procurement (DocuSign link to follow).
3) Kick off an infra checklist with Karthik for latency gating during pilot.

If this looks good I’ll produce the attachments and Mina can send to Alex.

— Ben
